items.title: LangGraph in production: Temporal's LangGraph Plugin adds Durable Execution
items.feed_description: LangGraph agents now run on Temporal: automatic crash recovery, free human-in-the-loop waits, and full observability via new LangSmith integration.
items.summary: Temporal announced a public preview release of its LangGraph plugin, enabling seamless integration of LangGraph agents with Temporal's durable execution platform. The integration allows LangGraph workflows to run without code changes, providing automatic failure recovery, human-in-the-loop steps, and long-running execution capabilities. LangSmith integrations for Python and TypeScript are also now in public preview.
features: Durable execution of LangGraph workflows via Temporal Workflows and Activities
Automatic failure recovery with checkpointed state resumption
Human-in-the-loop support with durable waits (signals/timers)
Long-running agent support with continue-as-new and state persistence
Compatibility with LangGraph's Graph API and Functional API
LangSmith integration for tracing across distributed workflows
items.why_it_matters: Developers can now deploy LangGraph agents in production with reliability, scalability, and observability, eliminating manual recovery and state management while maintaining their existing agent logic.

items.title: July 15, 2026
items.feed_description: Try the new Astro experience This feature is in Preview . Astro's navigation now gives you a single view across your entire Organization instead of a single Workspace. Deployments, Dags, and Astro IDE projects all appear across Workspaces in one view, with Workspace context on every row. Filter to a specific Workspace when you need to, or work from the full picture across your Organization. Workspace, Organization, and personal settings now share a single settings layout. The homepage also surfaces: Recently Failed Dags : An Organization-wide table of failing Dags, sorted by failure rate, with time-range filters. Each row shows the Workspace and Deployment, run history, and two actions: Investigate with Otto and Open in Airflow . Jump Back In : A strip of recently visited Deployments, Dags, data products, and Astro IDE projects. Favorite Deployments : An Organization-wide view of Deployment health with All , Healthy , and Hibernating status filters. Each card shows status, cluster and repository context, and four metrics: Dag Runs, Tasks, Worker CPU, and Worker Memory. You can favorite Dags (Airflow 3.1+) and Deployments to pin them to the top of these views and filter to only your favorites. Enable the new experience from the banner in Astro. To switch back, go to Your Profile , click Edit next to Astronomer Labs , and turn off the Astro Next toggle. Switching between experiences doesn't change your pipelines or configuration.
items.summary: Astronomer released updates on July 15, 2026, including new features like a unified organization view, Otto integration for code reviews, Sub-Second Pipelines for high-throughput workflows, and enhanced deployment analytics. Key changes also involve improved security, IP access list protections, and dag-level access control. The latest CLI, runtime, and agent versions are 1.42.1, 3.3-2, and 1.8.1 respectively.
features: Unified organization-wide view across Workspaces and Deployments
Otto integration for pull request reviews and Dag failure investigations
Sub-Second Pipelines for API-triggered Dag runs with <1s latency
Enhanced Deployment analytics with Kubernetes executor metrics
Favorite Deployments feature with health status filtering
Testing against existing Astro Deployments instead of ephemeral ones
IP access list protection against accidental self-lockout
Dag-level access control with role-based permissions
Environment Manager migration for connections/variables
Disaster recovery configuration moved to dedicated tab
items.why_it_matters: These updates improve collaboration, reliability, and security for data teams, enabling better workflow management, faster debugging, and centralized resource governance across deployments.

items.title: Why a context engine needs Durable Execution: How Unblocked rebuilt its ingestion backbone on Temporal
items.feed_description: See how Unblocked replaced bespoke ingestion orchestration with Temporal to run 1 million durable, observable AI context Workflows every day.
items.summary: Unblocked rebuilt its ingestion backbone using Temporal's Durable Execution to handle continuous, cross-source computation for its AI context engine. The migration replaced a custom actor model with Temporal's polyglot SDK and durable workflows, enabling resilience to failures and observability. The system now processes 1 million workflows daily across non-code data sources.
features: Durable Execution for continuous state computation across heterogeneous sources
Polyglot SDK support (Kotlin, TypeScript, Python)
Deployment-free workflows with automatic checkpoint resumption
Temporal UI replaces custom observability tools
Integration with Slack, Asana, CI systems, and other data sources
items.why_it_matters: Temporal's durable execution enables Unblocked to maintain accurate, real-time context for AI agents despite frequent system changes, improving reliability and reducing engineering overhead for orchestration plumbing.

items.title: Astro Observe data quality now in Preview
items.feed_description: This feature is in Preview . Astro Observe data quality for Snowflake and Databricks is now available in Preview. Data quality helps you monitor tables and columns for data quality issues including row volume changes, schema changes, and null columns, alerting on issues and displaying upstream and downstream table-level lineage to help keep your data accurate and complete. See data quality for setup and more information. Additional improvements Astro Observe SLAs now support flexible cron-based schedules to capture complex business logic and allow more control over SLA sensitivity.
items.summary: Astronomer released Astro Observe data quality in preview, alongside updates to Astro CLI (1.42.1), Runtime (3.3-2), and Remote Execution Agent (1.8.1). Key changes include enhanced Organization-wide views, testing against existing deployments, Sub-Second Pipelines for high-throughput workloads, and Otto integration for code reviews and failure investigations. The release also introduces improved analytics, security features, and DAG-level access control.

Test against existing Astro Deployments with configuration reuse

Otto automated code reviews and Dag failure investigations

IP access list protection against accidental lockout
DAG-level access control with role-based permissions
